title: Do Language Models Understand Igbo Culture? Beyond Multiple Choice
abstract: arXiv:2610.35168v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: The value of language models for any community depends on whether a model actually understands the culture of the people it intends to serve. We use the Igbo language as a case study. Existing benchmarks test translated Western ideas, lacking depth. To address this, we introduce CAB-Igbo, a benchmark developed from indigenous cultural sources and verified by native speakers across six domains. We evaluated diverse models under varying conditions, incorporating regional personas. Performance was assessed using multiple-choice accuracy and human evaluations across Epistemic Fidelity, Representational Richness, Linguistic Quality, and Pragmatic Proficiency. Results reveal a stark dissociation between language fluency and cultural knowledge. translated_title: 语言模型理解伊博文化吗？超越多选题
translated_abstract: 语言模型对任何社区的价值取决于模型是否真正理解它所意图服务人群的文化。我们以伊博语为案例进行研究。现有的基准测试考察的是翻译过来的西方思想，缺乏深度。为解决这一问题，我们提出了CAB-Igbo，这是一个基于本土文化来源构建、并由母语使用者在六个领域进行验证的基准测试。我们在不同条件下评估了多种模型，并纳入了地区性人格设定。性能通过多选题准确率和人类评估进行衡量，评估维度包括认知忠实度、表征丰富度、语言质量和语用能力。结果揭示了语言流畅性与文化知识之间存在显著的脱节。通过统计检验，我们发现对于大多数模型而言，认知忠实度和表征丰富度的严重缺失在英文中就已经存在，并且在切换到伊博语时并未显著恶化。
tldr: 本文提出了基于伊博本土文化构建并由母语者验证的CAB-Igbo基准测试，通过多选题与人类评估相结合的方式，揭示了语言模型的流畅性与文化知识之间存在严重脱节，且多数模型在英文中就已缺失认知忠实度和表征丰富度。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces CAB-Igbo, a benchmark grounded in indigenous Igbo cultural sources and verified by native speakers, revealing through multiple-choice and human evaluations a stark dissociation between language fluency and cultural knowledge, with most models already lacking epistemic fidelity and representational richness in English.
